calls.video_title: The Stock Market Is Crashing - What I'm Doing Now
calls.thesis: Construction Partners down 9% on short-term margin compression expected in H1 FY27, but nothing changed long-term; by 2030 it will be a significantly larger business. Buying more on the dip - an example of the market's short-term focus creating opportunity.
calls.base_case: Margins compress for ~6 months, then regain and grow by end of next year.
calls.bull_case: By 2030 ROAD is significantly larger and today's price looks ridiculous.
calls.bear_case: Margin compression lasts longer than the guided 6 months.

calls.thesis: Buying most aggressively; CEO owned the Q4 guide miss (diesel +40%, bad weather), FY27 guide of 15% revenue/EBITDA growth looks sandbagged with $290m acquired revenue already banked; ~8.3x trailing EBITDA, cheapest since the 2020 crash, 2030 targets $6bn revenue / $1bn EBITDA intact.

The 20% sell-off is a short-term overreaction to a wet Q4 and a diesel-price spike; FY26 revenue +30%, net income +40%, EBITDA +23%, and FY27 guidance still calls for ~15% revenue/EBITDA growth with margins re-expanding in H2 2027.
calls.price_at_call: ~$77/share (was ~$80, rallied to ~$100, fell back after preliminary Q4 results; down 20% on the day; 8.4x trailing-12-month EBITDA, below its 2022 bottom of 11.8x)
calls.base_case: 15% annual EBITDA growth, 13x EBITDA exit (below ~15x long-term median) -> 24.3% CAGR over 5 years.
calls.bull_case: Hits FY27 projections, ~$1bn EBITDA by 2030, back to 15x EBITDA -> 30% CAGR.
calls.bear_case: Only 10% annual growth and 10x EBITDA (a 33% discount to history) -> still ~13% CAGR.
